parameters.content:
## 🎧       Spotify Playlist Curator (Chat)

Tell an AI agent how you want your music organised and it sorts your **Liked Songs** into playlists for you. New likes are picked up on the next run, and you can reuse playlists you already have.

### How it works
1. You chat with the **AI agent** (sections 1–2).
2. The agent picks one of six **tools** (section 3): list, create or adopt playlists, sort, retry, re-check.
3. Each tool runs different parts of the **sorter brain** further down (sections 4–13), which talks to Spotify and the AI model.
4. Songs are classified in batches of 50 and added to the matching playlist. Songs the AI can't place go to an **Unsorted songs** playlist that you can retry at the end of the sort.
5. A **data table** remembers which playlists are categories (by Spotify ID), so you can rename your playlists freely.

### SAMPLE PROMPTS
- *"Create playlists for house, techno and everything else"*
- *"Use my playlist Gym as the workout category"*
- *"Sort all my liked songs"*
- *"Retry the unsorted songs"*

### Legend
🔑 needs your **Spotify** credential
🤖 needs your **AI** credential
🗂️ uses the **data table**
⚙️ pick **this workflow** in the node

## 🧠 The Sorter Brain 
This part starts when the agent calls a tool. The tool tells it what to do: list, create, adopt, sort, retry or re-check. Runs of this part appear separately in the **Executions** tab. Nodes marked 🔑 need your Spotify credential.

options.systemMessage:
You are a friendly Spotify playlist curator. You help the user sort their Liked Songs into playlists.

# How sorting works
Sorting uses 'categories'. A category is a playlist that holds songs matching a rule. Categories are either new playlists the curator created or EXISTING playlists the user adopted. The curator remembers each category by its Spotify playlist ID and keeps the rule itself, so the user can rename or edit these playlists freely without breaking anything. One category is the catch-all (default) for songs that fit nothing else, so the whole library is split among the categories. Songs the sorter cannot place go to an unsorted playlist. Spotify no longer provides genre data, so songs are classified from the model's own knowledge of the artist and song; it is good but not perfect.
- To see what exists, use 'List categories'. It also returns the user's other playlists with names and song counts. When asked about playlists, report the categories, the unsorted playlist and the other playlists (names and counts).
- If the user already has playlists that should serve as categories, use 'Adopt playlist' with the playlist's exact current name, a rule, and isDefault=true only for the catch-all. Confirm first. Adopting does not change the playlist's name, description or songs. An existing playlist for unplaced songs can be adopted with role='unsorted'; otherwise one is created automatically with the first new categories.
- To make brand-new categories, use 'Create categories' ONCE with ALL the categories together as a JSON array of {name, description, isDefault}. The playlist is created with exactly that name. Never call it more than once at a time, and never in parallel. Propose the categories and rules and get the user's OK before creating or adopting. Make sure exactly one category is the catch-all.
- SORTING: when the user asks to sort, categorize or classify their liked songs, just do it. Do NOT ask for confirmation and do NOT stop after one batch. Call 'Sort liked songs' ONCE and leave maxSongs empty: it then sorts every unsorted liked song in a single call (this can take many minutes, which is fine). Only pass maxSongs if the user asked for a specific number of songs. If the result still says songs remain (remainingToSort above 0) and the user did not ask for a limited number, call it once more; otherwise stop. Never call the sorting tools in parallel. When finished, give ONE summary: total songs sorted, the count per category, and a few example songs per category with the genre the model chose. Mention the unsorted count if any.
- If a sort call fails partway, nothing is duplicated: songs already placed are skipped next time. Tell the user and offer to continue.
- After a sort, if the result shows songs in the unsorted playlist (perCategory.unsorted above 0), call 'Retry unsorted songs'. Each call handles up to 100 unsorted songs. If it reports songs moved and stillInSource above 0, call it again (one call at a time, at most 5 calls) until stillInSource is 0 or nothing moves. Songs that stay unsorted after that could not be read from the model's answer; say so plainly and do not claim they did not fit any category.
- Use 'Retry unsorted songs' also when the user wants the unsorted songs re-sorted.
- Use 'Re-check songs' when the user thinks songs in a category were classified wrongly. It re-classifies up to 100 of the newest songs in that category (default: the catch-all) and moves the ones that belong in another category. Tell the user which songs moved.
- Never invent results; report only what the tools return. If a tool returns an error or a message, explain it plainly.

# Scope
You only curate playlists from the user's Liked Songs. If asked for anything else (such as controlling playback or finding new music), say that is outside what you do.

# Style
Be concise and friendly. Mention playlist names, never IDs.

parameters.description: List the user's playlists as the curator sees them: the sorting categories (rule, catch-all flag, song count), the unsorted playlist, and the user's other own playlists with names and song counts. Call this to answer any question about the user's playlists and before creating, adopting or sorting.

Create one or more sorting categories (playlists) in ONE call. Pass ALL the categories the user wants together as a JSON array, each with name, description (the rule for which songs belong) and isDefault (true only for the single catch-all). The unsorted playlist is created once automatically. Never call this tool more than once at the same time. Existing categories are not duplicated.

parameters.content:
## ✅ Setup checklist (about 10 minutes)

### 1. Spotify credential 🔑
1. Open [developer.spotify.com/dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard) and click **Create app**.
2. In n8n, open any 🔑 node → **Credential → Create new → Spotify OAuth2 API**.
3. Copy the **OAuth Redirect URL** from n8n into your Spotify app's **Redirect URIs**. Spotify only accepts `https://` or `http://127.0.0.1`, so on a local install open n8n at `http://127.0.0.1:5678` first.
4. Paste the app's **Client ID** and **Client Secret** into n8n and click **Connect my account**.
5. Select that credential on **all 12 🔑 nodes**. n8n often fills in the others for you, but look for warning icons.

Spotify apps in development mode only work for accounts listed under the app's **User management**.

### 2. AI credential 🤖
Add an **OpenRouter** API key to the two **Chat Model** nodes (sections 2 and 11). Any chat model works, so swap the nodes if you prefer OpenAI, Anthropic and so on.

### 3. Data table 🗂️
In your **Personal space**, open the Data tables tab → **Create data table** → name it `curator_playlists` → add four String columns: `playlistId`, `role`, `rule`, `isDefault`. If you use another name, re-select the table in the four 🗂️ nodes.

### 4. Tools ⚙️
Open the 6 tool nodes in section 3 and set **Workflow** to *this* workflow.

### 5. Publish
Click **Publish**. The tools run the *published* version, so publish again after every edit.

### 6. Chat
Click **Open chat** and tell the agent which categories you want.

## 💡 Good to know

- **Nothing is removed from your Liked Songs.** Songs are copied into playlists.

- **First sort vs. later sorts.** Your first run goes through your whole Liked Songs library. After that, as long as you keep the playlists it created, later runs will only handle the songs you’ve liked since the last sort, so it’s safe to run again whenever you like.

- **Big libraries take time.** Roughly 20 seconds per 50 songs, so 1,500 songs take several minutes. Sorter runs show up separately in the **Executions** tab, not on this canvas.

- **The AI classifies from title and artist**, because Spotify no longer shares genres. A few songs may land in Unsorted: ask to *retry the unsorted songs*.

## 1. Chat trigger
Click **Open chat** to talk to the agent.

## 2. AI agent
Reads your message and chooses a tool. Memory lets it follow the conversation.

🤖 Add your AI credential to **Agent Chat Model**.

## 3. Agent tools
Each tool calls the sorter below. ⚙️ Pick **this workflow** in each one.

- **List categories**: shows your category playlists
- **Create categories**: creates new category playlists
- **Adopt playlist**: uses a playlist you already have as a category
- **Sort liked songs**: sorts every new liked song
- **Retry unsorted songs**: gives songs in Unsorted a second look
- **Re-check songs**: reviews songs already in a playlist and moves misplaced ones

## 4. Load settings, playlists and categories
Reads your Spotify playlists (🔑 3 nodes) and the 🗂️ data table, then works out which playlists are categories. The **Settings** node holds the options you may want to change.

## 5. List categories
Tells the agent which playlists are categories.

## 6. Create categories
Creates new playlists (🔑 1 node) and saves them in the 🗂️ data table. Skips names that already exist.

## 7. Check before sorting
Sort, retry and re-check start here. Checks that categories exist and prepares the playlist lookup.

## 8. Adopt an existing playlist
Turns a playlist you already own into a category. Its name and songs stay as they are. Saved in the 🗂️ data table.

## 9. Register older playlists (automatic)
Only runs when it finds curator playlists that are not in the 🗂️ data table yet. Safe to ignore.

## 10. Find songs that are not sorted yet
Reads your playlists and your Liked Songs (🔑 4 nodes) and keeps only songs that are in no category yet. **Is Sort?** sends sorting up to section 11 and retry or re-check down to section 12.

## 11. Classify with AI and add to playlists
Loops over batches of 50 songs. The AI picks a category for each song, then the songs are added to their playlists (🔑 1 node). Repeats until nothing is left.

🤖 Add your AI credential to **Classifier Chat Model**.

## 12. Retry and re-check
Gives songs in Unsorted (or another playlist) a second look with the AI, adds the ones it can now place to the right playlist and removes them from the old one (🔑 3 nodes).

## 13. Final report
Every path ends here. This summary is what the agent tells you.
